title: Bipartisan Senate bill would push DOD to expand its oversight of in-use commercial frontier AI models
key_facts: Sens. Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.) proposed an 18-page bill, the Insider Threat Reporting and Security Guidance Act of 2026.
The defense secretary would have 180 days to issue reporting rules for 'covered' AI contractors, defined as companies with Pentagon AI deals of $100 million or more.
Companies would share security policies, who can access model weights and training, suspected incidents, unauthorised access and past evasions of safeguards.
They would certify the information is accurate at least every 90 days.
National security incidents such as theft of model weights must be reported within 72 hours; material vulnerabilities within seven days.
The Pentagon has 2025 contracts of up to $200 million each with four frontier AI firms and May 2026 agreements with eight companies that exclude Anthropic.
quote_evidence: A bipartisan bill proposed in the Senate would require the Pentagon to continuously vet the commercial tech giants from which it buys frontier AI for security vulnerabilities, algorithmic failures and other emerging risks accompanying the models that could compromise U.S. defense and national security.

Broadly, the bill would apply the Defense Department’s significant purchasing power to help enforce safety standards and transparency about the military’s AI use, ahead of Congress passing more sweeping industry-wide federal AI regulations.
why_it_matters_hint: The Pentagon would get a standing view of the security of the AI it buys.
